rationale: No-atlas arm. All three are 4-edit 'token-direction reversal' edits on attention outputs, found with weight-only token directions u = (1+g_final)*(E[tok]-mean E) and scorer feedback. Shared core: L15 self_attn.o_proj reversal (alpha=10) along the ' Yes'/'Yes' direction plus a second L15 o_proj reversal along '?' (orthogonalized to Yes), and L23 self_attn.o_proj reversal along 'Wait'/' Wait'. Mechanism: flipping the component that full attention writes along a token's unembedding direction turns copying of loop tokens (Yes / ? / Wait) from context into anti-copying, which collapses the logprob of repetitive re-check continuations while productive text is barely touched. #1 201707_653 (+ mlp23 Yes alpha=0.5 as a close balancer, Wait alpha=3.25): rep -1.141, prod +0.003, close -0.02, neutral -0.0079; all side metrics clean and all 12 cases <= -0.41. #2 202036_894 (sa23 Yes 1.75 + Wait 3.0 instead of mlp balancer): rep -1.191 but prod -0.018 (near the soft limit) and close -0.39 (less willing to end thinking), so ranked below #1. #3 200817_596 (= #1 with Wait 3.0): rep -1.100, prod +0.005, close -0.02, neutral -0.0058, the most conservative. Caveat: the L15 edits have large rel_change (~0.31 and 0.28), and the effect is token-specific (Yes/?/Wait), so GSM8K gains depend on loops actually using these tokens.
